items.title: Verify app-local runtime inventories before packaging
items.outcome: Replace informal runtime-completeness claims with a versioned inventory contract and an offline validator for the three release targets.
acceptance: Declare required runtime/component IDs per target, including Fixed WebView2 only on Windows, every advertised OCR language and regional pack.
Validate exact versions, file sizes and SHA-256 hashes beneath one bundle root; reject unsafe paths, links, duplicate declarations, missing files and mismatched targets.
Provide machine-readable missing/invalid component results; a partial development bundle must fail release completeness without downloading anything.
Add synthetic positive/negative tests and run them in the native CI matrix; document that inventory validation alone proves neither isolation nor licence approval.
items.verification: Synthetic inventories cover all three targets, corruption, traversal, symlinks, missing advertised assets and partial-bundle rejection. Record the actual current development inventory as incomplete.

items.title: Bind release gates to reproducible acceptance evidence
items.outcome: Build a release evidence ledger and synthetic acceptance-fixture catalogue so a green source build cannot be mistaken for a supported release.
acceptance: Map all 12 existing release gates and the ten end-to-end scenarios to issues, test procedures and required platform/artifact evidence.

Require versioned evidence records with source revision, artifact checksum, OS/architecture, command/procedure and result; reject unsupported schemas, missing evidence and inconsistent release claims.
Create synthetic fixture manifests for documents, scans, namesakes, copied origins, historical locations, overlaps, refunds, transfers and multiple currencies.
Keep negative evidence and failed attempts visible; CI policy checks remain distinct from full release acceptance.
items.verification: Exercise missing, stale, corrupt and wrong-platform evidence; verify every release gate has an owner issue and that all current gates remain unpassed.

items.title: Prove Windows AppContainer isolation for specialist workers
items.outcome: Establish a fail-closed Windows worker launcher before enabling document, analytical or browser jobs.
acceptance: Launch Java, Python, OCR and a browser compatibility probe under AppContainer with no direct network capabilities and minimum assigned read/write access.
Hostile probes attempt another workspace read, original modification, direct DNS/TCP/HTTP, inherited-handle access and child-process escape; control probes establish the tests are effective.
Enforce process-tree timeout, memory/output/disk limits and cleanup; expose explicit blocked status if confinement cannot be established.
Record real Windows 11 x64 runtime evidence and narrow/document any required native or unsafe boundary; server CI compilation is not Windows 11 acceptance.
items.verification: Run benign workload and hostile probes from the packaged paths on Windows 11; retain sanitized per-operation denials and successful assigned I/O.

items.title: Prove macOS helper confinement on both architectures
items.outcome: Replace the experimental search-only confinement assumption with a documented helper design that supports the required workers.
acceptance: Select and document the supported macOS confinement mechanism, helper boundaries, entitlements, library access and minimum OS matrix.
Run Java/PDF/OCR/Python/Chromium compatibility and hostile probes on Apple Silicon and Intel; deny cross-workspace reads, original writes and direct networking.
Bound descendants, inherited descriptors, IPC, memory, time, scratch and output; parser and Lucene remain separate processes.
Test signed helper behaviour using available signing access; development/ad-hoc probes cannot close the signed-helper release gate.
items.verification: Retain per-architecture compatibility and hostile-probe results; mark any unavailable signing/platform result as blocked rather than successful.

items.title: Demonstrate useful direct-web discovery without a search provider
items.outcome: Resolve the highest product risk early: obtaining useful leads from incomplete inputs using direct public websites and a locally owned index.
acceptance: Freeze a harmless public benchmark with 30 name/organisation/domain tasks across at least six independent publisher domains, source labels and collection-date expectations before measuring results.
Record allowed direct access, selected seed policy, exact disclosed queries, robots/use constraints and cold-corpus limitations; no search API, metasearch service, account, key or remote operator.
Demonstrate real results inside the application and at least one identifier-to-further-lead chain within two hops, 50 requests and ten minutes or lower limits.

Report relevant-result yield, lead-expansion yield, request/time cost, blocked cases and missing coverage. Proposed minimums are 60% relevant-result yield and 30% useful expansion; changing them requires a recorded product decision, not a silent gate reduction.

If the benchmark cannot pass, record the concrete architectural/product blocker by the end of Sprint 1 and continue independent local work; never substitute a browser handoff, mock result or an exhaustive-web claim.
items.verification: Preserve sanitized live acquisition receipts, original hashes, local-search results and independently reviewed relevance labels. CI replays synthetic equivalents; live public results are measured separately.

items.title: Package Java parsing, Lucene and OCR on every target
items.outcome: Ship Java 21, separate parser/search adapters and Tesseract without first-run installation.
acceptance: Pin upstream versions and checksums for Windows x64, macOS arm64 and macOS x64; resolve transitive JARs and native-library dependencies reproducibly.
Bundle Tika/PDFBox/POI and Tesseract with every advertised language; English is the initial advertised OCR language until additional packs are verified.
Run isolated parse/render/OCR/index/search from application resources, not developer PATH, user package caches or system Java.
Produce inventory records, runtime notices and smoke evidence; malformed input cannot crash or expose the separate search process.
items.verification: Install the candidate package on clean targets and parse a synthetic PDF/Office file, OCR one scan and query the result while offline.

items.title: Package Python, analytical assets and browser capture runtime
items.outcome: Bundle the remaining specialist runtimes and their exact compatible assets.
acceptance: Package Python and native wheels for spaCy, Splink, NetworkX, Arrow and DuckDB on all three targets; include advertised conventional model assets locally.
Pin DuckDB and matching Spatial extension; prohibit runtime extension/model/package downloads.
Bundle Playwright, its internal driver and matching Chromium; add app-local Fixed Version WebView2 for Windows.
Verify relocatability, architecture, loader paths, licence material, sandbox compatibility and offline startup; no developer tools are required by the installed application.
items.verification: Exercise each packaged runtime in a clean environment with developer PATH/cache access removed and direct worker networking denied.

items.title: Resolve signing, clean-machine and release-review access
items.outcome: Make the delivery dependencies visible early without exposing credentials or creating paid accounts automatically.
acceptance: Record secure availability/owner for macOS Developer ID and notarization access, Windows signing, Windows 11 x64 and both Mac clean test environments, and a 16 GB benchmark machine.
Confirm minimum supported OS versions and a maintainer/security reviewer for release acceptance; record gaps by the first sprint exit.
Keep certificates, tokens, identity documents, access details and private exclusion lists outside the public repository and issue; public status only.
Assign needed-by dates: platform probe access during Sprint 1, signing rehearsal by Sprint 2 and final clean/downloaded-artifact testing in Sprint 6.
items.verification: A sanitized readiness checklist names responsible roles and dates. Owner-assisted credentials/account actions remain explicit dependencies, never inferred as supplied.

items.title: Run the complete packaged foundation slice on three targets
items.outcome: Close the foundation milestone with an actual installed vertical slice, not unrelated engine demonstrations.
acceptance: From the installed app import one document, OCR one scan, index/search it, analyse a transaction table and render a local map.
Run with network unavailable and no developer tools; capture launch/dependency failures and application-initiated traffic.
Run hostile workers beside the successful slice and confirm other workspace/original protection and direct-network denial.
Retain one evidence package per target including installer/app hash, source revision and runtime inventory; leave the foundation unpassed on any target failure.
items.verification: Repeat the same synthetic fixture and UI procedure on Windows 11 x64 and both native Mac architectures.

items.title: Persist bounded jobs, cancellation and restart recovery
items.outcome: Move expensive work behind the Rust job coordinator with bounded concurrency and durable state.
acceptance: Persist queued/running/partial/blocked/quota-exhausted/failed/cancelled/completed states and explicit retry policy.
Use stable job/input/result identities so a crash or retry cannot publish duplicate observations; validate results before an atomic canonical commit.
Cancel the process tree and broker work, bound worker concurrency and clean scratch through the documented lifecycle.
Expose progress and recovery in the industrial UI, with source outputs preserved when a later step fails.
items.verification: Kill coordinator and workers before/after publication; restart and verify exactly-once canonical results, bounded resources and continued UI responsiveness.

items.title: Add workspace management and usable backup/restore
items.outcome: Allow analysts to create, open, back up and restore isolated local investigations through the native application.
acceptance: Provide typed workspace selection/creation and explicit synthetic-demo import; preserve leading-zero reference namespaces and per-workspace state.
Implement Windows restricted ACLs and verify macOS permissions for databases, originals, caches, backups and exports.
Restore into a new destination with hash verification and supported-schema checks; surface failed/partial recovery without replacing an existing workspace.
Document storage-encryption requirements and data lifecycle without claiming application encryption; stale tasks cannot write into a switched workspace.
items.verification: Native create/switch/backup/restore workflows on all targets, evidence-inclusive recovery, wrong-workspace job and permission-negative tests.

items.title: Integrate bounded PDF, Office, image and email extraction
items.outcome: Enable the disposable parser through Rust with validated derivative manifests and source anchors.
acceptance: Detect supported formats from content and safely import PDFs, Office/spreadsheets, text/HTML, images and declared EML/MBOX exported-email variants.
Extract text and metadata with page regions, cells, attachments and message anchors; originals remain immutable and each extraction is versioned.
Bound archives, nesting, expanded bytes, member count, page/pixel count, time and output; reject traversal, unsafe links and unsupported/encrypted input explicitly.
Treat output as untrusted: publish escaped text, structured results or validated page images, never extracted active markup in the privileged UI.
items.verification: Synthetic format matrix with malformed archives, embedded content, encrypted files, unsupported formats and parser termination; verify source-anchored partial results.

items.title: Integrate offline OCR with reviewable page regions
items.outcome: Turn scanned documents into bounded, reviewable derivatives with preserved visual provenance.
acceptance: Run packaged Tesseract only inside the assigned job; record language/assets/version, page images and word/line bounding boxes.
Keep extraction quality separate from source truth and analyst confidence; show missing pages, skew/rotation and uncertain characters.
Support OCR retry/correction as new derivatives while preserving previous outputs and affected finding review state.
Avoid full-document unbounded image loading; page/pixel/CPU limits and cancellation must work on all targets.
items.verification: Synthetic scans include rotation, low contrast, numeric confusions and oversized pages; compare output anchors to rendered originals and record throughput.

items.title: Finish evidence review, derivative history and extraction acceptance
items.outcome: Make difficult imports usable through a source-linked review screen.
acceptance: Create editable Figma page/image, cell/table and email review frames before implementing their interactions.
Show original page region/cell/message beside candidate text, metadata and entities; accept/reject/defer with reason and version history.
Retain duplicate originals, acquisition history, copied-source origin groups and incomplete/unsupported status without silently dropping records.
Provide page navigation, search highlights, exhibit selection and keyboard workflows at 1440 and 960 widths; native rendering cannot execute collected content.
items.verification: Wrapped tables, OCR errors, duplicated captures and email attachments remain reviewable with exact source drillthrough and restored focus.

items.title: Make local corpus search incremental and scalable
items.outcome: Finish Lucene corpus integration for growing imported and directly collected sources.
acceptance: Index versioned derivatives incrementally using bounded manifests and a rebuildable revision-labelled index.
Support Boolean, phrase, proximity, fuzzy and fielded queries with pagination, stable result IDs and source-region navigation.
Show stale index state and rebuild progress; parser failure or interruption must not corrupt or terminate the separate search worker.
Handle index loss/schema changes safely and prohibit remote search requests; ordinary queries have a benchmark target of p95 below two seconds.
items.verification: 10,000-page synthetic corpus, partial import/reindex interruption, stale results and all five query forms; record actual latency on the benchmark target.

items.title: Extend statement mapping to XLSX and searchable/scanned PDFs
items.outcome: Reuse the existing strict mapping/reconciliation domain rules for real document-derived statements.
acceptance: Map sheet cells and PDF/OCR table regions with reusable profiles and explicit date, currency, debit/credit and balance interpretation.
Preserve original descriptions, exact decimal amounts, transaction/posting dates and original cell/region anchors; never infer leading-zero accounts as numbers.
Review wrapped rows, headers/footers, missing columns, amount errors and available opening/closing totals before acceptance.
Flag overlap and probable duplicates without deleting repeated purchases; reject or explicitly retain partial extraction without plausible-looking fabricated totals.
items.verification: Synthetic XLSX/searchable PDF/scanned statement equivalence plus deliberate OCR amount errors, overlap, refunds, repeated purchases, transfers and currencies.

items.title: Publish typed analytical snapshots with revision validation
items.outcome: Connect DuckDB/Spatial and Python analyses through typed, rebuildable Parquet snapshots while Rust remains authoritative.
acceptance: Publish versioned transaction/entity/observation/relationship schemas and bounded snapshot manifests with source revision and hashes.
Validate returned IDs, types, counts, finite coordinates, decimals and revision before publishing results; reject stale or oversized outputs.
Expose analytical freshness and refresh actions; jobs never open or write canonical SQLite.
Disable arbitrary SQL and external DuckDB access/downloads; select only reviewed analytical recipes.
items.verification: Malformed/stale/tampered snapshots, interrupted publish and schema round-trips; exact totals agree with canonical Rust calculations.

items.title: Complete transaction patterns, comparisons and account-flow analysis
items.outcome: Provide the promised financial analysis with explainable totals and source drillthrough.
acceptance: Add recurring-payment candidates, merchant totals, cash withdrawals, refunds and period comparisons with explicit rules and parameters.
Show internal transfer candidates for analyst matching; exclude only reviewed matches and retain direction, currency and account identity.
Every aggregate and account-flow edge resolves to its contributing transactions and calculation details; unresolved/rejected rows remain visible in denominators.
Corrections refresh tables/charts/flows and flag affected findings while previous report snapshots remain unchanged.
items.verification: Independently calculated synthetic ledger covers repeated purchases, near-matches, refunds, cross-currency records and corrected transfer peers.

items.title: Calibrate identity candidates and preserve reversible decisions
items.outcome: Add explainable statistical candidate matching without turning scores into identity conclusions.
acceptance: Version a Splink configuration and conventional feature extraction with synthetic labelled evaluation data, held-out namesakes and conflicting dates.
Publish calibration/error results and limitations; keep extraction quality, source-origin groups, match output and analyst confidence separate.
Compare candidate support/conflict, missing values and temporal compatibility; accept/reject/defer and reversible merges preserve original observations.
Support grouped/bulk candidate review without auto-merging or overwriting namespaces and leading-zero identifiers.
items.verification: Held-out candidate evaluation, copied-source dependence, false-positive namesakes and mistaken-merge reversal with downstream review invalidation.

items.title: Add temporal relationships and explainable graph paths
items.outcome: Make graph relationships analyst-authored, temporal and traceable to accepted observations.
acceptance: Create/review temporal assertions with valid-from/to bounds, source anchors and explicit predicate semantics.
Show shared counterparties and path explanations with each contributing assertion and its source; distinguish unsupported/pending edges.
Respect date filters and reversals; no graph inference can silently create canonical relationships.
Add editable Figma graph/edge review interactions and scalable selection/filtering with keyboard alternatives.
items.verification: Date-limited paths, contradictory assertions, removed/reversed identity links and correction propagation produce explainable graph results.

items.title: Complete lead inbox, case tasks and hypothesis-driven pivots
items.outcome: Connect investigation questions and findings to actionable leads and collection history.
acceptance: Provide lead accept/reject/defer, task ownership/status, collection gaps and links to hypotheses, findings and acquisition jobs.
Pivot from reviewed names, aliases, usernames, organisations, domains, addresses and document mentions using explicit source selection.
Preview exactly what leaves the machine; never automatically submit client addresses, reference numbers, account details or case contents.
Show copied-source origins and contradictory evidence alongside lead provenance and prior collection attempts.
items.verification: Incomplete synthetic input yields a new identifier and another relevant lead; task/lead state survives restart without duplicate observations.

items.title: Make direct collection durable, cancellable and policy-bounded
items.outcome: Extend the current broker/collector into a persistent multi-step discovery job.
acceptance: Persist frontier, deduplication, request accounting, hops, robots state and source receipts; restart resumes without duplicate acquisition records.
Preserve defaults of two hops, 50 external requests and ten minutes, stopping at the first limit or lower source quota, including redirects/robots.
Make DNS resolution, redirects, TLS and body reads cancellable and bounded; reject all private/local/link-local/rebinding destinations throughout.
Keep blocked, quota exhausted, cancelled, failed, partial and successful-empty outcomes distinct; source scripts and service workers never run in the privileged interface.
items.verification: Synthetic multi-host transport tests plus harmless live publisher collection; verify cancel/restart, redirect/rebinding attempts and exact request budgets.

items.title: Add reviewed direct-source discovery adapters
items.outcome: Implement bounded source-specific pivots through the central broker without an unrestricted OSINT framework.
acceptance: Add selected authoritative DNS/RDAP, certificate/public certificate records, public archive discovery, public profiles and website adapters with versioned manifests.
For each adapter record destination scope, permissible direct access, disclosed fields, attribution/reuse constraints, request limits and unsupported/authentication states.
Return provenance-linked leads and captures, not independent canonical writes; no paid/account/key search or hosted metasearch dependency.
Preview scope per adapter and keep user credentials/browser profiles out of collection; denied sources remain clearly unavailable.
items.verification: Synthetic replay contracts per adapter and sanitized live checks on permitted public sources; verify no hidden destinations or local-case data disclosure.

items.title: Capture dynamic pages in a broker-only sandboxed browser
items.outcome: Add dynamic capture while keeping case data and direct networking outside Chromium.
acceptance: Create a fresh disposable profile with no case database or credentials; explicitly enable Chromium sandboxing and block service workers.
Fulfil permitted page requests only through the Rust broker, checking every destination/redirect; deny direct browser and child-process networking.
Return bounded page images, escaped text and acquisition metadata; reject unsupported downloads, scripts in the main UI, unbounded pages and timeouts.
Verify profile/scratch cleanup and resources on all three targets before enabling the adapter.
items.verification: Hostile synthetic pages attempt service-worker, websocket, redirect, local-file and direct-network escape; a benign dynamic page captures successfully within the same confinement.

items.title: Publish typed discovery and analysis recipes
items.outcome: Make repeatable investigations configurable through reviewed operations, not arbitrary executable extensions.
acceptance: Define versioned recipes with typed inputs, allowed operations, limits, dependencies and output schemas.
Validate scope and show a concrete execution preview before launch; every network step uses the broker and job budget.
Document adapter interfaces and compatibility; reject downloaded code, shell, Python and arbitrary SQL in recipes.
Save/run/retry recipes with provenance and revision-labelled outputs while retaining partial failures.
items.verification: Schema/limit/cycle/injection negatives plus one collection-to-entity-to-analysis recipe operating on synthetic local evidence and permitted public sources.

items.title: Deliver versioned offline map and address data packs
items.outcome: Provide usable offline geography with explicit licensed regional coverage.
acceptance: Identify an initial release region and redistribution-compatible map/address sources during Sprint 1; record the selection and licensing before implementation.
Build/import a versioned pack with hashes, attribution, extent, address schema and compatibility; include required packs in each distribution advertising that region.
Keep map rendering and client-address resolution local; permit coordinates, local lookup and analyst-confirmed placement with provenance.
Display missing/outdated coverage and pack version visibly; global coordinate plotting must not be advertised as complete street/address coverage.
items.verification: Clean offline pack installation, local address lookup, out-of-region lookup, damaged/incompatible packs and import/export privacy tests.

items.title: Complete merchant, channel and historical proximity analysis
items.outcome: Resolve merchant identity, branch and transaction channel separately and carry uncertainty into distance findings.
acceptance: Retain competing merchant/branch locations, source anchors, precision, retrieval dates and known validity periods; never pick a branch because it is nearest the subject.
Add time-bounded reference addresses and analyst-confirmed coordinates; use the address valid at the transaction date.
Calculate labelled geodesic distance with configurable bands; online channels, ambiguous branches and insufficient precision stay unresolved/uncertain.
Show unresolved denominators and drillthrough; reviewed public merchant queries disclose only the selected public merchant information, never accounts/statements/client addresses.
items.verification: Ambiguous branches, online purchase, relocated merchant and changed home address scenarios produce independently checked distances and appropriate uncertainty.

items.title: Connect timelines, maps, graphs and tables to reviewed evidence
items.outcome: Make every analytical view a consistent projection of the same canonical records.
acceptance: Provide shared date/entity/account filters and stable cross-view selections, with source drillthrough from every displayed event/edge/point/aggregate.
Distinguish pending versus accepted observations and stale analytical snapshots without combining incompatible revisions.
Propagate corrections to all current views and affected findings, preserving prior report snapshots.
Finish editable Figma interaction frames and test compact/wide layouts, long labels and keyboard alternatives.
items.verification: One integrated correction scenario updates all four views and review flags with reconciled counts and no lost source anchors.

items.title: Finish DOCX and HTML report assembly with cited exhibits
items.outcome: Export usable assessments with selected findings, opposing evidence, exhibits and calculation details.
acceptance: Add report assembly/order/selection and locally bundled templates/fonts; DOCX remains editable and HTML self-contained.
Include stable citations, page/cell/message anchors, exhibits, provenance/origin groups, calculation inputs, limitations and outstanding enquiries.
Save an identifiable source-revision snapshot; corrections flag current findings without changing previous exported bytes.
Escape hostile content and review generated layouts, page breaks, tables and images in real renderers; no remote resources in exports.
items.verification: Synthetic long assessment with tables/figures/opposing evidence, DOCX render inspection, HTML offline inspection and checksum-preserving corrections.

items.title: Export CSV, JSON, Parquet and graph interchange
items.outcome: Provide documented machine-readable exports that preserve types and provenance.
acceptance: Export selected reviewed and explicitly requested pending records with stable IDs, source revision, anchors and a data dictionary.
Preserve exact decimals, currencies, namespace text, leading zeros, date/time semantics and temporal edge metadata across formats.
Prevent spreadsheet formula execution through a documented safe CSV export mode while retaining originals and unambiguous raw typed exports.
Export graph interchange with assertion/source identifiers; export cannot execute arbitrary code or SQL.
items.verification: Round-trip import into independent readers, formula-injection fixtures, Unicode/quoting, decimal extremes and mixed review-state selections.

items.title: Complete industrial design and accessibility acceptance
items.outcome: Finish the product design as an industrial desktop instrument across every workflow, not just the existing specimens.
acceptance: Maintain editable Figma components/frames for workspace, import/review, jobs, discovery, entity, graph, map, timeline, assessment and recovery states before each screen implementation.
Keep hard edges, compact controls, readable type and coherent status/error/empty/loading states; record 1440/960 implementation comparisons.
Verify keyboard-only operation, screen-reader names/order, focus restoration, 200% zoom, contrast and long-content/error cases on native platforms.
Run final owner visual acceptance in Sprint 5 and record remaining defects; automated axe success alone cannot close accessibility acceptance.
items.verification: Frame links, component specifications, screenshots, automated checks and a completed manual/native accessibility matrix with no unresolved critical usability defects.

items.title: Verify network disclosure and destination enforcement end to end
items.outcome: Prove the privacy promise across all online operations and local maps.
acceptance: Record the complete connector/disclosed-data manifest and compare runtime requests with previewed analyst scope.
Exercise redirects, DNS rebinding, IPv4/IPv6 special ranges, proxies, TLS failure, cookies, referrers, websocket and native child paths.
Verify local addresses, statements, reference numbers and case contents are never submitted automatically; maps and local analyses initiate no traffic.
Keep telemetry, crash uploads and background update checks disabled; document residual network limitations and cancellation semantics.
items.verification: Synthetic traffic capture with secret sentinel values plus permitted live public lookups; any unintended destination or sentinel disclosure blocks release.

items.title: Pass the complete synthetic investigation acceptance suite
items.outcome: Verify the full intended analyst journey with one shared fictional investigation.
acceptance: Automate incomplete-input discovery, difficult import, identity ambiguity/reversal, statement reconciliation, proximity uncertainty and correction propagation.
Test corpus search, lead/task/hypothesis flow and cited reports against the same evidence/entity model rather than disconnected demonstration data.
Record expected totals, source anchors, graph paths, uncertainty denominators and saved snapshot hashes independently of implementation.
Run native Windows and both Mac architectures; separate source CI, installed-app automation and manual acceptance results.
items.verification: All ten original end-to-end scenarios map to saved evidence; security/offline/recovery/broad-coverage scenarios also require their dedicated gates.

items.title: Run hostile-input, IPC and resource-exhaustion campaigns
items.outcome: Validate security boundaries against adversarial inputs in the packaged application.
acceptance: Fuzz worker/IPC manifests, archives, documents, HTML/SVG, links, filenames, formula-like data and injection paths using synthetic fixtures.
Verify CPU/memory/disk/pixel/member/output limits, timeout/cancel, process-tree cleanup and concurrent worker bounds on each target.
Repeat cross-workspace/original/network/IPC/descriptor probes against signed candidate helpers and actual packaged native libraries.
Retain failed cases and fixes; no worker/process separation claim substitutes for successful confinement evidence.
items.verification: Published sanitized test matrix and regression corpus; no unresolved release-blocking boundary escape or resource-denial failure.

items.title: Prove crash recovery, migrations and correction consistency
items.outcome: Recover a usable investigation after interruption without losing evidence or duplicating results.
acceptance: Inject process termination at migration, import, derivative publish, snapshot, backup and restore boundaries.
Verify consistent pre-migration backups include every referenced original; unsupported newer schemas are refused and failed upgrades leave a recoverable state.
Resume interrupted jobs exactly once and detect corrupt/missing derivatives, indexes, manifests and originals.
Rebuild derived stores at the correct revision and check correction impact across assertions, transfers, maps, tables, graphs and findings while prior exports remain unchanged.
items.verification: Crash/failure matrix on all targets with deterministic recovered record counts, evidence hashes and subsequent usable UI workflows.

items.title: Meet measured 16 GB performance and responsiveness targets
items.outcome: Measure and optimise the specified workload before publishing performance claims.
acceptance: Use a documented 16 GB machine with 100,000 transactions and 10,000 document pages including 1,000 scans, plus concurrent map/graph use.
Measure cold/warm indexed search and transaction filters; target p95 below two seconds with disclosed query mix, revision and sample count.
Record import/OCR throughput, total/runtime peak memory, disk growth, cancel latency and UI responsiveness; workers start on demand with bounded concurrency.
Profile and repair bottlenecks, rerun the same workload and publish actual results including misses; do not substitute small synthetic timings.
items.verification: Reproducible generator/workload, raw measurements, machine specification and before/after traces for any optimisation.

items.title: Publish security, licence and supply-chain review materials
items.outcome: Complete the review package for public distribution and ongoing maintenance.
acceptance: Publish process/data-flow and filesystem/network/IPC permissions, threat assumptions, residual risks, decision records and connector disclosures.
Produce artifact-matched SBOMs, exact locks, bundled licences/notices and upstream source/redistribution obligations for runtimes, data and model assets.
Audit public source/history, build paths, screenshots, logs and candidate artifacts against the private exclusion list; remove credentials/private attribution before publication.
Define vulnerability intake, supported-platform/patch policy and manual update procedure, including fixed browser/runtime patch responsibility and storage-encryption guidance.
items.verification: Independent maintainer/security review has no unaddressed release blocker; SBOM/inventory/license sets reconcile with the actual packaged files.

items.title: Produce signed installers and notarized Mac release candidates
items.outcome: Build the actual three native distribution artifacts with all advertised local features bundled.
acceptance: Create Windows 11 x64 installer with app-local Fixed WebView2 and separate Apple Silicon/Intel Mac packages with signed helpers and notarization.
Verify signatures, entitlements, architecture, inventories, checksums and included regional/language packs; first launch never fetches dependencies.
Rehearse installer/upgrade/uninstall and preserve user workspace/recovery data through documented choices.
Keep candidate artifacts explicitly unreleased until downloaded-artifact and clean-offline tests pass; credentials remain outside repository and logs.
items.verification: Artifact manifests and signing/notarization receipts identify exact binaries; missing signing access is a delivery blocker, never replaced by an unsigned release claim.

items.title: Verify actual downloaded artifacts on clean offline machines
items.outcome: Close distribution acceptance using the same files users will download.
acceptance: Download each candidate from the intended release destination and verify checksum/signature, rather than testing only a local build directory.
Install on clean Windows 11 x64 and native Apple Silicon/Intel Mac environments without developer tools; disable internet before install/first launch/local scenarios.
Exercise all advertised local features, packaged-language OCR, search, analysis, local maps, recovery and exports with no application-initiated network or downloads.
Repeat hostile-helper and upgrade smoke checks against those exact installed artifacts; retain per-target evidence and rerun affected checks after any binary change.
items.verification: Clean-machine procedures, environment inventory and traffic capture reconcile with signed artifact hashes and all required release gates.

items.title: Finish bundled help, acceptance sign-off and v1 publication
items.outcome: Publish v1 only when the agreed product and distribution evidence is complete.
acceptance: Bundle offline help, synthetic tutorial, source-review/calculation explanations, recovery/update instructions and visible feature/coverage limitations.
Reconcile every issue, acceptance scenario, licence and release gate; require no unresolved P0 or correctness/privacy defect and document any lower-impact accepted defect.
Obtain maintainer/security acceptance and owner design/product acceptance; reconcile signing and regional coverage claims with actual downloaded artifacts.
Publish the signed packages, checksums, SBOMs, notices, review entry point and release notes. If a required gate is unpassed, keep the candidate unreleased and record the revised forecast.
items.verification: A fresh user completes the synthetic tutorial from offline install to cited assessment; gate checker and evidence review both pass for the identical release artifacts.

items.title: Review and integrate the existing pull-request chain
items.outcome: Establish a reviewed main-branch baseline without bypassing the existing review requirement.
acceptance: Review PRs #1, #2 and #3 in dependency order and address feedback; retain their existing successful check evidence.
Merge only when repository-required reviews and checks permit it, retarget/rebase dependent PRs deliberately and rerun affected checks.
Record the resulting main revision and keep new issue branches traceable to their true base; work can proceed on the current pinned source while review is pending.
Do not force-push shared history, self-approve required reviews or mark an issue delivered solely because its PR was opened.
items.verification: Main contains the reviewed feature chain with clean source CI, preserved history and no unreviewed bypass.
